Of the 33,14,032 electors issued notices over lack of mapping or logical discrepancies in Delhi’s draft electoral roll, 31,26,576 (94.34%) have been cleared for inclusion in the final roll, the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) said on Tuesday.
Among the 19,34,243 cases involving logical discrepancies, 98.05% have been disposed of. The remaining cases are expected to be settled shortly, the CEO’s office said.
Officials said the office had prioritised the disposal of notices over the past two weeks, ahead of the November 30 deadline for settling notices, claims and objections under the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR).
Meanwhile, 2,67,441 Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in the electoral roll were received between August 31 and October 26.
Of these, 25,510 were received at special camps held at 14,947 polling stations on weekends between September 20 and October 25. Camps at educational institutions received 1,706 applications, while those organised for homeless people, transgender persons and sex workers received 549.
The draft roll, published on August 31, contained 97.53 lakh electors, down from 1.45 crore before the revision. During the house-to-house enumeration exercise, 47.56 lakh electors were left out, having been categorised as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, or for not submitting their enumeration forms.
The deadline for filing claims and objections is October 30, while the final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on December 4.
